name: Single-Leg Standing Calf Raise
summary: A unilateral bodyweight isolation movement performed standing on one foot to strengthen the gastrocnemius and soleus.

setup: Stand tall on one foot on a flat surface or with the ball of the foot on the edge of a step.
Bend the non-working knee slightly so the opposite foot hangs freely behind you.
Lightly touch a wall or sturdy rail with one hand for balance if needed.
steps: Press through the ball of the working foot to raise your heel as high as possible.
Pause briefly at the peak of contraction while keeping the working knee straight but not hyperextended.
Lower the heel under control until it lightly touches the floor or reaches a full, comfortable stretch below the step.
Complete the target repetitions, then switch to the other leg.
instructions.breathing: Exhale as you press up onto your toes; inhale as you lower your heel.
cues: Push straight through the big toe
Squeeze the calf at the top

common_faults.fault: Bouncing out of the bottom of the movement using the Achilles tendon rebound.
common_faults.correction: Pause briefly at the bottom of each repetition to ensure muscular work rather than elastic recoil.

common_faults.fault: Rolling the ankle outward onto the pinky toe.
common_faults.correction: Distribute pressure evenly across the ball of the foot, driving primarily through the base of the big toe.

common_faults.fault: Bending the working knee to assist the lift.
common_faults.correction: Keep the working leg locked in a straight position with only a micro-bend to fully load the gastrocnemius.

precautions: Maintain light fingertip contact on a wall or rail to prevent loss of balance.
